reviews.comment: Definitely depends on whether or not you have a lenient TA. Lectures are super boring and long. He definitely cares about his students. Make sure to redo turn-ins; it's basically what the tests are over. 80% weight on tests (7 of them), so make sure to do well on those. The cheat sheet helps but doesn't replace not knowing the material.

Very difficult to understand at first but he provides outside sources to help you understand the material. He loves questions and students coming up with their own unique solutions. He is genuinely a sweet professor. The grading is solely dependent on the TA following a rubric set in place so if you get a really strict TA your grades may look scary
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class is difficult due to it being very test heavy, with exams only having two to three workout problems. Lectures can also feel pretty long. However, I think overall Dr. Mercier sets up his students well for success in future classes.
Very smart guy.

This is a tough class, but his teaching is fair and reasonable. There are 7 exams, which helped reduce my anxiety by the third test. He allows cheat sheets, offers lots of office hours, plus TAs and SI sessions. There's plenty of support if you struggle, and overall, he's a really sweet guy if you get to know him.

His lectures are very boring. Though, his in-class examples are good and he posts them after class. The grader was lenient on tests. There are six midterm tests which I liked cause it was only two free response questions so it felt like biweekly quizzes. The final was hard. Request from ASCE test bank to practice for tests.

A very sweet guy, and I enjoyed him a lot. For each of the seven tests, you should request his past tests from ACSE. Without them, I would have failed. He doesn't drop any tests unfort. Jeff Hanson on YouTube can help a ton. Our grader was pretty leanant. My grade is not necessarily his fault, but I did put in a lot of time to get a mid one (C).

7 tests is kinda rough, but it's helpful for staying on top of things. The final was pretty hard, but the rest of the tests are fair as long as you have concepts down. The graders tend to be pretty lenient so small mistakes don't drag you down much. Some of the weeks had way too much hw (10+ hours) while others were pretty light.
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Do not have a semester over 12 hours with this class. If u commute, its a very bad idea. Time spent in his classroom maybe useless for some. Jeff Hanson video was the only thing that helped me. HW, study and assignment time spent a week was 16 hours and it doesn't help; his test questions aren't what was mentioned in class or HW.

I put more hours into this class than any I've ever taken. I was in the upper quartile on every exam and still barely passed. The tests were extremely difficult. Only 1.5 points were curved. So many failed. The TA seemed to want us to fail. I lost 62.5% on a question for one missed negative sign.Other sections exams where easy compared to this guy.

Mercier is AWFUL-You will have 7 exams, an exam every other week, and the exams will be significantly more difficult than other profs (Nearly every exam had a failing average). He goes over slides in class, and rarely explains the underlying concepts in depth. Most students end up teaching themselves the material outside of class. Grading is strict
Very tuff class, there is easier options for those taking 305/221 , save yourself the trouble and take someone else. Very smart guy btw.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Unfortunately, Prof. Mercier was an awful teacher and this was a hard class. Seven tests over the course of the semester which the TA grades and he never looks at, so he doesn't know what students are struggling on. Doesn't curve, no extra credit, and is baffled when students are doing bad. Half of my  class failed. Nice guy, bad prof, don't take.

This man is a piece of work. You get an exam basically every other week and when our whole class failed all the test he blamed it on us not being as smart as his past students rather then considering that he or the graders caused the problem. He's patronizing and was blatantly mean to students who asked questions. I would recommend someone else.

The class is so hard but he's a good prof. He knows everyone's names and really cares. He's not an easy A tho and you'll do a lot of work but you'll really learn the material. I had him for 221 and 305 and I really loved him. I personally kinda sucked at this class tbh but I don't blame him. He's awesome. Great sense of humor too.
nice professor, very smart! gotta lock in though

Dr. Mercier is a really great professor; a lot of the reviews here don't do him justice. It's a tough class no doubt, but he does everything he can to make the class manageable. Tests are often but are over less content, which is very helpful for statics. The HW and turn-ins are time consuming, but they supplement your studying. He definitely cares

His lectures were a bit dry but they covered all of the material so that if you did the homework and payed attention in class, you will be fine on the test. Old exams available if you join the group me. Don't expect an A though only 12% of our class got one.

SEVEN tests make up 80% of the grade. Pay attention or else you will struggle in this class. Multiple homeworks every week and an additional assignment every other. Methods can be found on chegg. you get a cheat sheet for the tests that gets bigger every test. he posts lecture slides and example problems on canvas.

Good professor for 221, can't say the same for 305. Your test grade will depend on the TA, but the problems will not be like class examples (since he didn't make his own slides) or the online hw (pointless, get chegg). His average GPA for the class was a 2.9.

Dr. Mercier's style is hit or miss. There are a lot of tests that make the class very time-consuming but also make studying easier since you only need to go over a few lessons. The graders vary every semester in harshness so just pray you have nice ones. This class can be challenging but if you watch Jeff Hanson on YouTube you should be fine.

Fun fact, Mercier will take up a majority of your time at school. Guess what? You get an exam every other week (6 exams + 1 final) no curves and no mercy even if the class fails. You will also consistently have online assignments (2 hours each) along with turn-in assignments (3-5 hours each) every other week. Lastly, get chegg, it's your only hope.

Lectures are very monotone. Yes, I realize this perhaps can't be helped with statics, but he couldn't make it any more boring. Tries to encourage participation with sporadic questions. Isn't super helpful with assignments and in office hours it feels like he can't wait for you stop asking him questions. Maybe it's just my perception
Chegg makes a profit on professors like him.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He teaches hard classes but he is a good professor
The exams are nothing like what is discussed in class. Be ready to fail

The lectures are useless and often he goes too fast for you to understand what'd going on. The homeowork is nothing like the lectures and you will be expected to magically know it even though he has never taught it. Wish I never took him. There's 6 exams each worth 10%.

Statics isnt the easiest class but he makes it straightforward. 6 exams and a final which sounds bad but only two topics on each exam. trust me its better than the other prof. he teaches it well and is very accessible if you have questions, turn in assignments can be hard but graded easily. practice his notes and use ASCE test bank and you are good

6 exams and a final sounds like a lot, but each exams covers small amount of material so easy to study for which is nice. Lectures can be pretty boring, but if you have questions he will help you and he is also super helpful in office hours. Turn in assignments usually are similar to exam, and turn ins and exams are graded very easily.

Mercier is awesome. his lectures were really boring and monotone, but he would explain the concepts in clear detail. Test heavy with 6 exams and a final but it helps you study and prepare better. very kind and approachable and willing to hop on zoom after work hours to help explain concepts. very easy grader as well and gives lots of partial credit

Lots of exams, basically one every other week. Lots of homework too, but if you do it after class like the syllabus shows, it's not too bad. He's super nice and fun to get along with. Posts all notes on canvas. Lots of resources for tutoring and help outside class too. Course material can be a little tricky, but take good notes and you'll do good.

He is overall a really good professor for CVEN 221. He has many tests which means that if you do bad on one, you have 5 more instead of the tests being worth 30% each. He is very engaging in his lectures and in his examples and he always explains everything very well and will slow down or speed up as long as you communicate with him.
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: it's a 2-hour lecture, it's hard to stay engaged the entire time regardless of the teaching style. He is a great teacher to take for 221. weekly homework and biweekly worksheets. quizzes (in lieu of not having major exams) cover material learned the previous week(s). grades well as long as you show you know and have learned the material.

So far, he has been the worst professor I have had at TAMU in terms of his lecture. He just reads off the slides and does the bare minimum. Sitting through his lecture without falling asleep is a challenge in itself. If you do take this class, get a Chegg account because you won't be learning from him.

Mercier had very bland and monotoned lectures but he works through what you'll see on the exam. He gives lots of partial credit on exams, and you have 6 exams, not including the final. Exam every 2 weeks with only a couple of topics so its relatively easy to study for. If you can make it through the lectures you can do well.

He is very strict, but at least you know what to expect. He has A LOT of tests and no extra credit of any sort. His lectures are boring and he is very monotone. One good part of his class is his completed notes are very detailed and he explains his thought process. This class is just a generally difficult class, so he is an okay professor overall.

Mercier was a great professor for 221. If you show up to class and listen to his lectures (which can be dry sometimes) you will do just fine in this class. He gives a LOT of tests but it helps give you a stable grade and means you don't have to memorize a lot of material you just need to practice often. I highly recommend him!
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: There are 6 tests 10% each. you dont really have to go the only thing that is helpful is the example problems and he posts the solutions. theres reviews monday nights that are helpful. but other than that not a super helpful class. invest in chegg.

Professor Mercier teaches a tough class, but does it really well. He knows his stuff super well, and is super happy to walk you through, even step by step, any question that you may be stuck on. He tests often (6 per semester), but they're only two questions, and they are never curve balls. Very similar to things you will of worked in class.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The only reason Dr. Mercier has such a low rating is because of the difficulty of his class. He is awkward but also cool in his own way. I had him for CVEN 221 and his tests are often twice as difficult as example problems he does in class and that is the only reason he did not get a 5/5 from me. GO TO CLASS.

Dr. Mercier is a nice guy and statics in general, is just a hard class. He does his best with helping out the grades by allowing cheat sheets on exams and having lots of exams. That being said most of the learning you do will definitely be outside of class. Jeff Hanson will become your best friend.

When I was unfortunate enough to have Dr. Mercier, it was his first time teaching 305, and it was online as well. His lectures are twice a week, 2 hours each of an incredibly monotonous walkthrough of pre-written slides. None of his prep material or homework were relevant to the tests; nothing I could study could give me full readiness for them.
reviews.ratingTags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Mercier wasn't a fantastic lecturer but he is very smart and is a very nice guy if you put in the effort to get to know him. Class was very test heavy, but tests were graded leniently with heavy partial credit. The lectures are boring and long and he does a lot of examples, but he tells you what questions/topics will be tested.
He is a good person, but if you don't learn through example you will have a very difficult time learning in his class.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: For the love of God, don't take this man. Statics is an essential class for civil engineering, and you're not going to learn it from him. Majority of the students relied on outside resources to learn the material. His tests are crazy hard, and all he does is read off the slides in class. I can easily say he's the worst professor i've ever had.
reviews.ratingTags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Mercier is a solid prof for statics. He covers plenty of problems in class that are similar to homework and test problems. He allows students to work together on assignments and allows cheat sheets for tests. Would highly recommend getting a regular study group for this class, watching Jeff Hanson on Youtube and going to office hours.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Mercier has a bad rap. He is a nice guy. His lectures are dry, to say the least. His class consists of 20 Online hw, 10 Turnin hw, 4 major quizzes, and 3 tests. The quizzes are 1-2 questions. The tests are 4 questions. he allows cheat sheets for quizzes and tests. If you can get a hold of one of his old tests they help with studying

Dr. Mercier is not a great lecturer BUT he is super helpful when you ask specific questions in office hours or class. The exam questions are over in-class examples and turn-in assignments. I would say not to even bother studying the online homework. This class is not easy but ask for help when you need it and you should do well!!

Hard clas but doable. 4 one question quiz:5%each, 3 four question tests:20% each. 10%online hw, 10% turnin hw. Plan to spend 6+ hours each week outside of class. Tests hard but are from the TURNin hw and lectures. Ask prof questions after class and during lectures to fully understand. He explains things well to those who want to learn. Good person
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He makes you work for your grade. There is partial credit which is extremely helpful. He is always open for questions and typically gives a thorough explanation. The example problems he provides tend to be more helpful than the online homework. You have to really know the material because exam problems tend to be more complex.

Mercier takes advantage of being the only professor for this class. Because of this, he can basically do whatever he wants for this course and it is obvious. Its doable, however it is extremely hard, and outside resources are a necessity if you want to pass. Take this class VERY seriously and ask questions during class, and you can do it.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lots of work for this class. Going to class is important. Lectures aren't the best. Prof is caring and friendly tho. Lots of the material will be self-taught through working examples on your own. Tests have quite a bit of partial credit.

He wasnt the best lecturer but this was his first time teaching the course and he was always looking for good feedback to improve his teaching. He also would answer any question (no matter how simple).

Awful lecturer. Static physics isn't too hard, but that's once you understand the stuff. In order to understand how to do problems, you have to see them worked out - he doesn't work them out in front of the class; he has a PDF with all the worked out steps for a problem that he just lectures from and then expects you to magically understand.

Terrible lecturer. Only teaches by briefly explaining problems from typed solutions prepared before class. Assigns extra turn-in HW every week (on top of the standard 2 weekly online HW assignments) that are extremely difficult and aren't like any example problems from class/the book. Test questions aren't like any HW/example problems. DO NOT TAKE!

He is not a very good lecturer. Most people who go to class don't even pay attention. I would NOT take him again he is extremely boring and gives out almost three assignments a week. His tests are pretty hard and we have no way of studying but reading the whole book.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK
